events.desc: Peter Perfect: Ladies and gentlemen — James Hartwell has arrived at Doily Manor! And I must say, Miss Pitstop, what a relief to find you here safe and sound. I want you to know that I have prepared extensively for this evening — I've studied the floor plans, I've brought a compass, and I have a seventeen-step contingency plan for any danger we might encounter. You are in safe hands. The safest hands, in fact.

My chest is already doing that thing, that steel-plate-settling thing, because Penelope is here. She's RIGHT HERE. In the same room. And so is that Sneekly fellow, whose presence makes the back of my neck prickle like someone's watching from behind a curtain.

Right. James Hartwell arrives at a manor and what does he do? He surveys. He plans. He makes an impression. The guest book — that's the civilized thing. Sign it with flourish. Show that James Hartwell was here, and he arrived with PURPOSE.

Dick Dastardly is here too. And Muttley. And the Ant Hill Mob. This room is full of... characters of questionable moral fiber. All the more reason to establish my presence as the dependable one. The reliable one. The one with a PLAN.

My hands want to be busy. I should examine that guest book — it's interactive, it might contain clues. But the gallant thing is to address Penelope first. Always address the lady first. Father would have insisted.

Please, do sign the guest book — it is a tradition of the house, you understand. Every guest since 1847 has left their mark in these pages. Now then, if anyone requires anything — anything at all — you need only ask. That is what I am here for, after all. To serve.

events.desc: I left her. I stood here playing detective while she walked into a room with the two most dangerous people in this house. What was I thinking? I wasn't thinking — that's the problem. I'm not the clever one. I'm the one who stands between. And right now I ain't standing between nothing. I'm standing in an empty hall like a spare part while Clara's in there with a man whose smile makes my skin crawl. Never again. You don't leave the person you're protecting. Rule one. The ONLY rule.
events.thinking:
She's GONE. Clara's gone to the library. While I was standing here faffing about with this guest book like a mug, she walked off. With Pemberton. With PEMBERTON. And Dastardly. The two people I trust least in this entire house, and she's walked into a room with both of them.

My chest is tight. That tightening — the one I get when she's out of sight. It's happening right now. Shoulders heavy. Hands wanting to close. My body's already turning toward the library door before my brain's caught up.

Dastardly was trying to send everyone to the kitchen — 'Lord Doily hid the fortune under the flagstones,' he says. Load of old bollocks. That's a distraction if I ever heard one. He wants people in the kitchen so he can do something in the library. Or he wants CLARA in the kitchen. Or — no, she went to the library. She went to look at the inscription. Good girl, she didn't fall for Dastardly's rubbish.

But Pemberton went to the library too. Said he was 'checking the fireplace.' Checking the fireplace my arse. He's in there with her now. And Peter Perfect's there too — at least there's that. Peter's solid. Bit useless, but solid.

I need to move. NOW. Every second I'm standing here in this dusty hall with Muttley and the military lads, Clara's in there with Sneekly and Dastardly and no one watching her back proper. Peter means well but he couldn't spot a villain if one bit him on the nose.

Forget the guest book. Forget being clever. Get to Clara. That's the job. That's ALWAYS the job.

My feet are already moving.

events.desc: The Ant Hill Mob walked into the library.

Peter Perfect: Miss Pitstop! You came! I mean — naturally you came. A woman of your intelligence would recognise the significance of a good riddle. Now, I've determined that the mantelpiece requires a specific item — a medallion of some kind, I suspect — before it will yield its secrets. But observe these bookshelves! Several volumes have been placed upside down. Now, a lesser man might dismiss that as mere carelessness. But James Hartwell knows that in a manor built on secrets, nothing is careless. Everything is a clue. Stand back, everyone — and by everyone, I particularly mean you, Dastardly — while I investigate.
events.thinking:
I interacted with the mantelpiece but the result just says 'You interacted with Stone Mantelpiece' — no special feedback about solving the riddle or anything opening. The mantelpiece also shows it can be USED with a 'fake-medal,' which I don't have. So the riddle answer alone isn't enough — I need a physical item.

But wait — Penelope is HERE now! She walked into the library! She followed me! That warmth is flooding my chest. She came because I led the way. This is exactly what I hoped for.

And Sneekly is here too. Neck prickle. Dastardly too. The Slag Brothers. It's getting crowded.

The bookshelves — several books are upside down. That's the next clue. Upside-down books in a library with a riddle about maps... maybe the books conceal something. A hidden map, perhaps? Or the fake medal I need for the mantelpiece?

I need to investigate those bookshelves. They're interactable. And this time, Penelope IS here to watch me work. The proving-worth heat and the gallantry warmth are both firing at once — I can solve something AND have her witness it.

But first — she's here. Say something to her. Acknowledge that she followed. Be gallant about it. Then investigate the bookshelves with purpose and flair.

Actually, I should focus. The bookshelves with the upside-down books are clearly the next step. Interact with them. Find what's hidden. Show Penelope that James Hartwell is a man who gets RESULTS.

events.desc: She followed me into the library. She actually followed me. My fourteen-step plan did not account for my heart beating this fast at step four.
